query: For high-entropy-alloy coatings used in wear-resistant applications, what single intervention could improve wear resistance across operating temperatures? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its expected mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise identical unmodified coating, the temperature and sliding conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of titanium to high-entropy alloy coatings will improve their wear resistance across operating temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy coatings without titanium addition
generation.intervention: Addition of titanium to the high-entropy alloy coatings
generation.conditions: Operating temperatures above 800 °C, sliding conditions with increased load, velocity, and distance
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of protective oxides, solid-solution strengthening, and dispersion strengthening
generation.mechanism: The addition of titanium causes solid-solution strengthening and hence increased strength and hardness, leading to improved wear resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance of the high-entropy alloy coatings with titanium addition compared to those without titanium
generation.baseline: Wear resistance of high-entropy alloy coatings without titanium addition
generation.boundary: Operating temperatures below 800 °C, sliding conditions with low load, velocity, and distance
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of titanium addition required for optimal wear resistance, the potential formation of brittle phases with high titanium content

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test with high-entropy alloy coatings with and without titanium addition, operating at temperatures above 800 °C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate of the high-entropy alloy coating with titanium addition is not significantly lower than that without titanium, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: One of the most investigated HEA systems is AlCoCrCuFeNi and the copper-free derivate AlCoCrFeNi [,]. Distinct improvement of mechanical properties can be achieved by alloying with titanium. Due to its large atomic radius, the addition of titanium causes solid–solution strengthening and hence increased strength and hardness. Additionally, the formation of brittle phases was observed for a high content of titanium [,,]. The wear resistance of the alloy system AlCoCrFeNiTi has been investigated under various conditions revealing an increased wear resistance, also in comparison with the steels EN 1.3505 and EN 1.3343 [,]. Although improved high-temperature properties of AlCoCrFeNiTi are expected, the wear behaviour has not yet been investigated at increased temperature.

The investigations prove the suitability of AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 for high temperature applications. Due to the formation of protective oxides, an improvement of wear behaviour occurs. Further investigations have to be conducted to determine the wear behaviour under different wear conditions. The influence of the additional σ-phase has to be investigated in subsequent studies.

40Cr steel has excellent strength, stiffness, and plasticity and is extensively employed in mechanical parts, such as midload gears, crankshafts, and oil pump rotors. Wear is one of the primary failure modes of 40Cr steel in service. Wear consumption results in a large amount of energy and material consumption. Enhancing the wear resistance of parts has attracted considerable attention. Generally, heat treatment can be used to enhance 40Cr steel’s wear resistance, but owing to the process’s complexity and difficulty in controlling time and temperature, it will waste energy [,,,,]. Laser cladding, an advanced surface modification technology, is crucial for rapidly heating and curing metal powder into coatings using a high-energy laser to repair and enhance the surface of parts [,]. Laser cladding has special advantages such as a low dilution rate, low thermal impact, a fine cladding layer microstructure, and a good metallurgical combination compared with other technologies [].
